newsitem.title: USA: Localities with yield burning probes may network.
newsitem.headline: Localities with yield burning probes may network.

text.p: Government Finance Officers Association will help states and localities that are subjects of federal yield burning probes to contact each other, a GFOA official said on Tuesday.

Catherine Spain, head of GFOA's federal liaison center in Washington, made the pledge at the group's annual convention here after a Pennsylvania county controller said she wants to "network" with other municipalities being investigated by the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Yield burning refers to allegations that bond underwriters overcharged states and localities in recent years for U.S. Treasury securities purchased to help refinance outstanding bonds.
SEC officials have said that the agency has over 20 yield burning probes underway.
Judith Kraines, Berks County, Pa. controller, said she has several bond issues underwritten by Meridian Capital Markets that have been the subject of SEC subpoenas.

CoreStates Capital Markets, a unit of CoreStates Financial Corp, which purchased Meridian after the underwritings, has pledged to help localities pay yield burning settlement costs with federal agencies.

"My concern is that the municipal voice be heard," Kraines said. "We've been told that this will be worked out between underwriters and the SEC or Internal Revenue Service and I wonder where the municipal voice is heard."
Kraines said four Berks County governmental units got SEC subpoenas, among them the Reading, Pa. School District and Reading, Pa. Parking Authority.

Spain said GFOA has not been contacted by many localities under investigation. She said GFOA will publish a notice in its upcoming newsletter to members urging municipalities that want to share information to send a contact name to GFOA. The association will then make the names available to other localities upon request. She said names will not be made available to the press.
